content.text:
I submitted index 136 (Cr 0.10, Fe 0.63, V 0.27) as the best composition. Its EQE was 0.149%, the highest of the three compositions I measured. That used the whole merit budget (3). I never measured XRD, so all 5 XRD measurements were left unused.

| Index | Composition (Cr / Fe / V) | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 136 | 0.10 / 0.63 / 0.27 | **0.149** |
| 90 | 0.10 / 0.46 / 0.44 | 0.097 |
| 128 | 0.36 / 0.26 / 0.38 | 0.088 |

- **Model results:** MACE puts FeVO4 (mp-504509) at 0 eV/atom above the convex hull, so it is stable. MEGNet predicts its HSE band gap at 2.75 eV, just above the 2.72 eV illumination, so it would absorb that light poorly.
- **Why Fe-rich helped:** My explanation is that the Fe-rich film also contains Fe2O3, which has a band gap of about 2.1 eV and absorbs 455 nm light better. I didn't check this with XRD, so the phases in that film are unconfirmed.
- **Order of measurements:** I started at an FeVO4-like composition (index 90), then tried a Cr-rich one (index 128), which did slightly worse. I spent the last measurement on the Fe-rich side (index 136), which gave the best result.

**Limitations:**
- **Coverage:** Only 3 of 201 compositions were measured, so a better one may well exist elsewhere in the library, for example at even higher Fe or in the V-rich corner.
- **Phase list:** The full phase list was too large to return, and I had no tool to read the saved file. I checked only the one phase ID I could find.
- **Last pick:** My third pick went against the GP model's suggestion, which was index 117 (Cr 0.19, Fe 0.40, V 0.40).
